contribution: Separates novel-combination generalization from compositionality; Appendix8.4 manipulates input density while fixing sampled combination count.
evidence_summary: Official ACL2020 full text read, especially Sections2–6 and Appendix8.4/8.7. 10000 sampled meanings,100/140/200 values,90/10 split,all values train-visible; density-sensitive generalization. Symbol-position interventions additionally distinguish highly generalizing yet entangled languages.
novelty_comparison: For v30, fixed six-value degree-two supports and a common degree-two held H12 narrow the question beyond support density. Connectivity, four-cycles, local Cartesian product structure and training distance vary together; an isolated connectivity mechanism is not established. No directly isomorphic prior was found in this bounded four-query review.
recommendation_reasons: Must cite before claiming a new experience-support effect.
Directly rules out equating high unseen-combination J with compositional syntax.
concerns: One-hot inputs and supervised receiver differ from frozen visual/private-action agents.
Only successful training runs are used for generalization analyses; density also changes attribute cardinality.
summary: Direct prior that combination coverage affects generalization independent of sampled input count, and that functional generalization does not establish compositional syntax. v30 should compare matched supports and conditional whole-message interventions without rebranding this earlier coverage result as new.
